solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shoot nuisance outside a capital of Europe

indicators.note: outside tells us the shoot-and-nuisance pair sits around the little word a

parts.note: a shoot on a plant is a bud
a nuisance is a pest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to gun down a pest lurking near a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the shoot and the nuisance around the A, which falls where the two pieces meet. 'Shoot' reads like a command to fire a gun, but here it is a plant shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary, so it is one of Europe's capitals.

clue.text: One employed to serve member in company of outlaw

indicators.note: in company of means the limb sits within the outlaw word

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
an arm is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A gang employs someone to wait on them alongside a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlaw' reads as a bandit but is the verb ban; 'member' is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman is employed behind a bar to pour and serve drinks.

clue.text: Satanist controversy was brought up by dispatcher

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a row is a controversy
lived can mean existed, so was
a shipper dispatches goods

explanation.surface: A devil-worship scandal is raised by a delivery company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns ROWLIVED to give DEVILWOR, then SHIPPER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Satanist worships Satan, the Devil, which is what the compound describes.

clue.text: Headless corpse developed holes in skin

indicators.note: developed means the remaining letters are made into something new
Headless means the word corpse loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a decapitated body has broken out in blemishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' leaves ORPSE, which 'developed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Pores are the tiny openings in the skin through which sweat escapes.

clue.text: Conventional curved structure used in farm feature

indicators.note: used in puts the curved structure inside the farm building

parts.note: a sty, for pigs, is a feature of a farm
an arch is a curved structure

explanation.surface: A traditional archway is incorporated into a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts the curved structure inside the farm feature. 'Conventional' reads like a description of the arch, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy means stiff and formal, as starched clothes are, so rigidly traditional.

clue.text: Merchant returned colour works of creative imagination

indicators.note: returned means the colour and the creative works are read back to front as one run

parts.note: red is a colour
art covers works of creative imagination

explanation.surface: A dealer sends back paint and paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns REDART round as a whole, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is someone who buys and sells goods, which is what a trader does.

clue.text: Transplanted retina, stored in wine, is prepared for a new role

indicators.note: stored in means the mixed letters go inside the wine

parts.note: red is wine

indicators.note: Transplanted means the letters of retina are moved around

explanation.surface: An eye surgeon keeps a donor retina in wine before reassigning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transplanted' turns RETINA into TRAINE, which sits between RE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be retrained is to be taught new skills ready for a different job.

clue.text: Weird customer kept iPod disconnected from one electronic organiser

indicators.note: Weird signals that all the letters are rearranged
disconnected from removes the letter for one from the device name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A strange shopper held onto a music player unplugged from the mains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconnected from one' leaves POD, mixed by 'Weird' with CUSTOMER and KEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop computer organises files, data and diaries electronically on a desk.

clue.text: Work on racket and break band

parts.note: a rest is a break
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: Bust a group of criminals and their noisy operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests crime, but it is a tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Restringing a tennis racket means fitting it with new strings.

clue.text: Odd bits of rust appearing in display switch

indicators.note: appearing in places the chosen letters inside the word for display

parts.note: to display something is to reveal it

indicators.note: Odd bits of picks the first and third letters of the word rust

explanation.surface: Patches of rust show up on a switch on a control panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits of' takes R and S from 'rust'; 'appearing in' puts them inside REVEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch can mean a change to the opposite, which is a turnaround or about-face.

clue.text: Instruction to move on family member's eyelid problem

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to move on to the next page
a sister, sis for short, is a family member; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A relative's droopy eyelid prompts a note to turn the page.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO (please turn over) is printed at the foot of a page to send the reader on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptosis is the medical term for a drooping upper eyelid.

clue.text: Cut jade

definitions.meaning: a jade is a worn-out old horse

explanation.walkthrough: 'jade' looks like the green stone but is an old nag.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is both a rough chop and a hired, tired riding horse.

clue.text: The first cervical vertebra is shortened eventually

indicators.note: shortened says the phrase for eventually loses its final letter

parts.note: eventually means at last

explanation.surface: A medical fact: the top neck bone gets shorter in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' drops the last T from AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomists name the topmost neck bone, holding up the skull, after the Titan who held up the sky.

clue.text: Contract broken by a cold person

indicators.note: broken by means the contract word is split open with the new letters inside

parts.note: a charter is a formal contract or deed
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chilly individual breaks an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' splits the contract word in the middle so that the A and the cold letter can sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Character can mean an individual, especially an odd one, as in 'a shady character'.

clue.text: Soft brave not supported by leader of tribe

indicators.note: not supported by means the brave word goes without the letter named next

parts.note: doughty is an old word for brave and steadfast

indicators.note: leader of picks the opening letter of the word tribe

explanation.surface: A warrior lacks backing from the chief of his people and grows soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of tribe' gives T, removed from DOUGHTY. 'brave' looks like the warrior noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughy describes something pale and yielding like unbaked bread dough, hence soft.

clue.text: Guy after gear manipulated elderly relative

indicators.note: after places the mocking word behind the mixed gear
manipulated means the letters of gear are worked into a new order

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or taunt them

explanation.surface: A man follows equipment being operated by an old family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb to mock. 'manipulated' turns GEAR into GREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, typically an older family member.

clue.text: Family doctor concerned with key issue

parts.note: kin are family
GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor in Britain
in can mean concerned with, as in 'in shipping'

explanation.surface: A family physician deals with a crucial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is the British family doctor seen first for any ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the central or most important element, so the crux on which everything depends.

clue.text: Find sound recording too much

parts.note: a disc is a sound recording
over means excessively, as in overdone

explanation.surface: Learn that a record is excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to come upon it, to locate it.

clue.text: Closely look at cricket, perhaps, plugged by Pakistan's opener

indicators.note: plugged by means the next letter fills a gap inside the creature

parts.note: a cricket is one example of an insect, signalled by perhaps

indicators.note: opener picks the initial letter of Pakistan

explanation.surface: Study a cricket match featuring Pakistan's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the sport, but it is the chirping bug. 'plugged by' puts P inside INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine carefully, scrutinising something up close.

clue.text: Juvenile positions supported in private enterprise

indicators.note: positions supported in suggests letters held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A young person holds posts backed in a private business.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle 'privaTE ENterprise'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teen is a teenager, a young person not yet adult.

clue.text: Equipment used to broadcast entertainer's final farewell

indicators.note: final picks the closing letter of entertainer

parts.note: adios is Spanish for farewell

explanation.surface: A performer bids goodbye over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' takes R from 'entertainer' (the 's adds no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Radios are sets that transmit or receive broadcasts, so pieces of broadcasting equipment.

clue.text: Way left open to retain batting order

indicators.note: left open to retain means the way is split to hold the next piece

parts.note: a route is a way
in is cricket for batting

explanation.surface: A road kept clear to keep the batting line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting order' is a false cricket phrase; 'order' alone is the definition. ROUT(IN)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed sequence or regular arrangement of actions.

clue.text: Stiff coach rolled over in hospital unit

indicators.note: in places the turned vehicle inside the hospital unit

parts.note: a bed is a unit of hospital capacity

indicators.note: rolled over means the coach word is turned round

parts.note: a car is a railway coach

explanation.surface: A coach overturned, leaving someone stiff in a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled over' turns the vehicle backwards to give RAC, and 'in' puts that inside the hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Braced means rigid, held firm by supports or tensed against impact.

clue.text: Mint added to cocktail of a true liqueur

parts.note: to mint money is to coin it

indicators.note: cocktail of means the following letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A sprig of mint goes into a drink made with an orange liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' reads as the herb but is the verb for making money; 'added to' joins COIN to the mixed letters of A TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured spirit, a well-known brand of liqueur.

clue.text: Participants in choreography, perhaps, may be extraordinarily energetic

indicators.note: Participants in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dancers in a routine might be bursting with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for overexcited or highly strung, full of nervous energy.

clue.text: A radius shown in the redrawn central part

indicators.note: shown in places the pieces inside the rearranged word
redrawn means the letters of the are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A geometry diagram has a radius shown in the redrawn centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redrawn' rearranges THE to give HET, and 'shown in' puts A and the radius letter inside that, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the core or centre of something, as the heart of the matter.

clue.text: Mist's volume measured by a stream

parts.note: taken as written
to stream is to pour

explanation.surface: Fog rising beside a brook is gauged for its quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Mist's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is a fine suspension of water droplets, a form of airborne moisture.

clue.text: Informative one caught after accomplished performance

indicators.note: after sends the single letter and the caught letter behind the accomplished performance

parts.note: to have accomplished something is to have done it
an act is a performance
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An educational talk where someone is dismissed after a polished show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the one-and-caught pair behind the performance, although the clue names them first.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to teach or instruct, conveying information or a moral.

clue.text: Find beam, crossing river with it

indicators.note: crossing means the beam spans the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discovering a girder spanning a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' looks like a verb but is the noun: a rare find. RA(R IT)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A find is a valuable discovery, and a rarity is something uncommon and prized.

clue.text: Proudly displayed a roll nearly finished during meal

indicators.note: during places the shortened pieces inside the meal

parts.note: a feed is a meal
taken as written

indicators.note: nearly finished says the roll word loses its final letter

parts.note: a roll, as of a ship, is a turn

explanation.surface: A bread roll was almost gone during dinner, then shown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly finished' drops the last letter of the roll word, giving TUR, and 'during' puts A and TUR inside the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is featured it is given prominence or showcased.
